faqs.a: Yes. We'll come look at your roof, take photos, and give you a written quote. There's no cost and no pressure to sign.

faqs.q: How do I know if I need a new roof or just a repair?
faqs.a: It depends on the age of the roof and how widespread the damage is. A few missing shingles or one bad spot can usually be repaired. If the roof is old and has problems in many places, replacing it is often the better use of your money. We'll show you photos and explain both options.

faqs.q: How long does a roof replacement take?
faqs.a: Most homes take one to three days. Bigger roofs, steep roofs, or a lot of rotted wood under the shingles can add time. Weather can also push the schedule, and we'll keep you posted if it does.

faqs.q: Will my insurance pay for a new roof?
faqs.a: If your roof was damaged by a storm, like hail or wind, your policy may cover some or all of it. It depends on your policy and what the adjuster finds. We can document the damage and meet with your adjuster, but your claim is between you and your insurance company.

faqs.q: Do I need to be home while you work on my roof?
faqs.a: No. Many homeowners go to work like normal. We'll want to talk with you before we start and walk the job with you when we're done.
We work in {{city}} and across the {{region}}. If you're not sure we come out to you, just give us a call and ask.

faqs.q: What should I do if my roof is leaking right now?
faqs.a: Move things away from the drip, put down a bucket, and take photos. If water is near lights or outlets, turn off power to that area. Then call us so we can tarp or patch it and stop more damage.

faqs.q: How long does a roof last?
faqs.a: A regular asphalt shingle roof often lasts about 20 to 30 years. Metal roofs can last much longer. Hail, wind, poor attic airflow, and how well it was put on can all shorten that.
